chat_history.content: This global UpSet plot shows pairwise overlaps ranked by IoU across all selected channels, with the visible page (offset 9, showing 7 entries) spanning IoU values from ~0.47 down to ~0.46. The dominant visible overlap is SOX10+COX-IV (IoU 0.47, overlap_coeff 0.90), indicating that nearly the entire COX-IV mitochondrial signal is spatially embedded within the SOX10-positive melanocytic tumor compartment — consistent with COX-IV being a housekeeping organelle marker concentrated in metabolically active tumor cells. SOX10+B-tubulin (IoU 0.47, overlap_coeff 0.86) and SOX10+Catalase (IoU 0.46, overlap_coeff 0.83) show similarly high overlap coefficients, suggesting these cytoskeletal and antioxidant signals are also predominantly confined to the SOX10+ tumor cell population rather than distributed across the broader tissue. MHC-I+SOX10 (IoU 0.47, overlap_coeff 0.67) is notable because its lower overlap coefficient relative to COX-IV implies MHC-I is expressed on tumor cells but also extends into non-SOX10 populations — consistent with MHC-I upregulation on stromal or immune cells. Globally, the full dataset is overwhelmingly dominated by SOX10 and MART1 co-combinations, confirming a melanocytic tumor-rich microenvironment; Ki67, the active channel for proliferation, does not appear among the top overlaps, suggesting proliferating cells represent a minority subpopulation within the SOX10/MART1 tumor mass.
